decisions.decision: The finite latent-shift SCM is encoded as a parametric record `LatentShiftSCM E U W X Y` over five `Fintype`/`DecidableEq` index types, carrying the six primitives as functions/matrices (`pi : E -> Real`, `S : Matrix U E Real`, `M : Matrix W U Real`, `a : X -> U -> Real`, `f : X -> Y -> U -> W -> Real`, `q : U -> Real`) TOGETHER with the two induced laws `PM : E -> U -> W -> X -> Y -> Real` and `QM : U -> W -> X -> Y -> Real` as separate fields, AND with the NORMALIZATION of all eight objects as further proof fields: `pi_nonneg`, `pi_sum : sum_e pi e = 1`, `S_nonneg`, `S_col : forall e, sum_u S u e = 1`, `M_nonneg`, `M_col : forall u, sum_w M w u = 1`, `a_nonneg`, `a_col : forall u, sum_x a x u = 1`, `f_nonneg`, `f_col : forall x u w, sum_y f x y u w = 1`, `q_nonneg`, `q_sum : sum_u q u = 1`, `PM_nonneg`, `PM_sum : sum_{e,u,w,x,y} PM e u w x y = 1`, `QM_nonneg`, `QM_sum : sum_{u,w,x,y} QM u w x y = 1`. Two immediate consequences are proved in the same file as plain finite-sum lemmas: `observedLaw_nonneg`/`observedLaw_sum : sum_{e,w,x,y} observedLaw Mdl e w x y = 1` and `targetProxyVector_nonneg`/`targetProxyVector_sum : sum_w targetProxyVector Mdl w = 1`. Everything here is scaffolded over Mathlib `Matrix` / `Finset.sum` only, with NO measure-theoretic import; the conversion of these normalized finite laws into `Measure`s is F1-D11.
decisions.why: The note's every object is a finite matrix (column spaces, ranks, singular values, `B_x = M R_x`, `b = M q`) and every proof is finite linear algebra plus a positivity perturbation. Carrying `PM`/`QM` as fields rather than defining them by the product keeps `ass:latent-shift-factorization` and `ass:target-mechanism-invariance` non-vacuous Props exactly as the note atomizes them (they are `used_by` the class and by two theorems), instead of collapsing them to `rfl`. The normalization fields are the TYPE-LEVEL content the core's own symbol table already declares (`pi` a probability vector on `E`, `S` and `M` column-stochastic, `a` and `f` stochastic kernels, `q` a probability vector on `U`, `P_M` and `Q_M` probability laws on their product spaces): they belong to the world, not to any `ass:` node, so carrying them as record fields absorbs NO assumption atom -- strict positivity `0 < .` remains ass:strict-primitive-positivity and def:positive-latent-shift-class keeps exactly its four core members. They are load-bearing for this revision: without them `observedLaw Mdl` and `targetProxyVector Mdl` are raw real arrays and there is no probability law for `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample` (whose population argument has type `Measure X`) to sample from, which is precisely the S1/S2 world-type defect this round fixes. See substrate_survey for the bypass justification against `Causalean.SCM.Model.SCM` and `Causalean.PO.ID.Exact.Proximal.POProximalSystem`.

decisions.decision: REPLACED IN ROUND 4 (core revision). The former node `def:studentized-projection-handle` no longer exists in the core, and its Lean object is NOT retained as a node. What thm:no-uniform-studentized-wald-adaptation quantifies over is the note's own phrase `every sequence (C_n) of measurable data-dependent nonempty subsets of [0,1]`, realized as a plain (non-node) helper in `Helpers/TriangularArray.lean`: `structure ConfidenceSetSeq (Omega : Nat -> Type) where set : forall n, Omega n -> Set Real; nonempty : forall n omega, (set n omega).Nonempty; sub_unit : forall n omega, set n omega subseteq Set.Icc 0 1; meas : forall n (vartheta : Real), MeasurableSet {omega | vartheta in set n omega}`. The companion predicate is `UniformArrayCoverage (C) (p x alpha) : Prop := 1 - (alpha : Real) <= Filter.liminf (fun n => Causalean.Stat.coverageInfOrOne (fun A : studentizedArrayClassSet p x => (rowLaw A n).real {omega | rowInterventionalProb A n x y in C.set n omega})) Filter.atTop`. NO procedure `Type`, no recipe `String`, and no `IsSubsetUnitInterval` predicate survive: the subset condition is now a field of the structure. ROUND-7 AMENDMENT (core revision, F1-D19): the core now fixes the sample space of a row rule EXPLICITLY -- `C_n : Omega_n -> {C subseteq [0,1] : C nonempty}` with `Omega_n = Omega(ns n, nt n)` carrying its FULL POWER-SET sigma-field -- and states outright that such rules `are measurable because Omega_n carries its full finite power-set sigma-field`. The `meas` FIELD IS THEREFORE DELETED. The structure becomes `structure ConfidenceSetSeq (E W X Y) (ns nt : Nat -> Nat) where set : forall n, Omega (ns n) (nt n) -> Set Real; nonempty : forall n omega, (set n omega).Nonempty; sub_unit : forall n omega, set n omega subseteq Set.Icc 0 1` -- its index type is now the core's own `Omega_n` rather than an abstract `Omega : Nat -> Type` -- and the derived lemma `confidenceSetSeq_measurableSet : forall (C : ConfidenceSetSeq E W X Y ns nt) n (vartheta : Real), MeasurableSet {omega | vartheta in C.set n omega}` is emitted beside it, proved by `Set.Finite.measurableSet` (`Omega ns nt` is a `Fintype` with `MeasurableSingletonClass`). Every site that previously cited the `meas` field now cites that lemma; `UniformArrayCoverage` is otherwise unchanged. The conclusion's Hausdorff-deviation event is NOT required to be measurable: it is bounded below through `MeasureTheory.measure_mono` from the measurable event `A_n INTER G_n`, and `Measure.real` of a non-measurable set is the monotone outer measure, so no measurability hypothesis beyond `meas` (which is exactly what the note's `A_n = {5/8 in C_n}` step needs) is imposed.
decisions.why: The note no longer ASKS for a procedure; it PROVES an impossibility against every admissible confidence-set sequence, so the object to formalize is the universally quantified sequence, not a candidate constructor. Carrying `nonempty`, `sub_unit` and pointwise `meas` -- and nothing else -- is exactly the hypothesis surface the core sentence states (`measurable data-dependent nonempty subsets of [0,1]`); adding any further regularity would weaken the theorem, and dropping `meas` would make the note's own event `A_n` meaningless. Routing the final Hausdorff event through `measure_mono` rather than through an extra measurability field keeps the theorem as strong as the note states it: the bound holds for every admissible sequence, including ones whose deviation event is not measurable. ROUND-7: the core now supplies the measurability itself, from the power-set sigma-field of the finite row space, so retaining `meas` as a FIELD would be the mirror image of the round-3 defect -- an assumption standing where the core states a consequence -- and would make the theorem read as conditional on a regularity the core says is automatic. Deriving it is both faithful and free, and pinning the structure's index type to `Omega (ns n) (nt n)` is what makes the derivation available at all (an abstract `Omega : Nat -> Type` has no finiteness to appeal to).

decisions.decision: The rank-`r0` truncated SVD `H_{r0}` and its pseudoinverse `H_{r0}^dagger` are BUILT LOCALLY from Mathlib's Hermitian spectral decomposition of the `m x m` Gram matrix `H H^T`: with `U` the eigenvector unitary and `lambda_j` the eigenvalues taken in NONINCREASING order, `P_{r0}^star(H) := U_{r0} U_{r0}^T` is the orthogonal projection onto the top-`r0` left eigenspace, `H_{r0} := P_{r0}^star(H) * H`, and `H_{r0}^dagger := H^T * U_{r0} * diag(lambda^+_{r0}) * U_{r0}^T`. `sigma_{r0}(H)` reuses Mathlib `LinearMap.singularValues` on `Matrix.toEuclideanLin H` through a total, ONE-BASED wrapper whose argument IS the note's rank index: `sigmaAt (r0 : Nat) (H : Matrix W E Real) : Real := if 1 <= r0 then (Matrix.toEuclideanLin H).singularValues (r0 - 1) else 0`. So `sigmaAt r0 H` is the `r0`-th LARGEST singular value (Mathlib index `r0 - 1`, ordered by `singularValues_antitone`) and `sigmaAt 0 H = 0` is an unused sentinel, the core's rank index always satisfying `1 <= r0`. Mathlib's `LinearMap.singularValues` is a FINITELY SUPPORTED function `Nat ->_0 Real`, not a `Fin (min m |E|)`-indexed family (loogle, round 9), so it is already total on `Nat` and vanishes past the rank: `singularValues_of_finrank_le` gives `sigma_j = 0` for `j >= |E|` directly, and for the `m < |E|` corner the same vanishing at `j >= m` comes from `isLowerSet_support_singularValues` plus `rank(H) <= m`. The core's convention `sigma_{qbar+1}(H) = 0` for `qbar = min(m,|E|)` is therefore INHERITED rather than imposed, and is recorded as the small side lemma `sigmaAt_eq_zero_of_gt (h : min m |E| < r0) : sigmaAt r0 H = 0` -- no `dite`, no `Fin` coercion, no partiality anywhere. ROUND-9 CORRECTION (FLAG-sigma-index): the round-4 plan specified a ZERO-based `Fin`-indexed wrapper (`if h : j < min m |E| then singularValues (Fin.mk j h) else 0`), which was wrong twice over -- it mis-stated the Mathlib type, and, fatally, it made every consumer writing `sigmaAt j` for the note's `sigma_j` read `sigma_{j+1}`. At `r0 = 1` the two-case test `sigmaAt (r0+1) H < sigmaAt r0 H` then compared `0 < sigma_2` in place of `sigma_2 < sigma_1`, driving the impossibility theorem's own rank-one baseline `H_{x,0}` (`sigma_1 = 1/2`, `sigma_2 = 0`) into the fallback `0` branch and collapsing the Wald benchmark; it also made `ass:regular-singular-gap` bound the wrong singular value. Under the one-based wrapper the core condition `sigma_{r0}(H) > sigma_{r0+1}(H)` is RETAINED VERBATIM as `sigmaAt (r0+1) H < sigmaAt r0 H`, and the baseline lands in the derivative branch (`sigmaAt 2 H_{x,0} = 0 < 1/2 = sigmaAt 1 H_{x,0}`). Every `sigmaAt` consumer in this plan -- def:regular-wald-functional, def:regular-wald-variance, ass:regular-singular-gap, and `gap_of_mem` in def:strongly-identified-submodel -- is stated against this one-based reading, and the spelling lemma `sigmaAt_succ : sigmaAt (j+1) H = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin H).singularValues j` is emitted beside the definition so no downstream proof re-derives the `Nat`-subtraction arithmetic. ROUND-4 ADDITION: the core now demands a FIXED, possibly noncomputable SELECTOR of an orthonormal eigenbasis of `H H^T`, ordered by nonincreasing eigenvalue, with one fixed choice inside every tied eigenspace. Mathlib's `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvectorUnitary` composed with the antitone eigenvalue ordering IS such a selector: it is a single global (choice-based, noncomputable) function of `H`, so `phi_{r0}` is single valued at tied cutoffs by construction, with no `Set`-valued fallback and no `Classical.choice` introduced per call site. Two lemmas are now emitted beside the construction, because the core states them and the delivered theorem consumes them: `truncation_selector_independent : sigmaAt (r0+1) H < sigmaAt r0 H -> forall two admissible selectors, the retained subspace, P_{r0}^star H and H_{r0} agree`, and the local regularity fact `phi_{r0}` and `fderiv phi_{r0}` are continuously differentiable on the strict-cutoff-gap region, via the resolvent projector `P_1(H) = (H H^T - lambda_2(H) I) / (lambda_1(H) - lambda_2(H))` that the note's own proof displays.
decisions.why: Mathlib has ordered singular VALUES (`LinearMap.singularValues`, `Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.SingularValues`, confirmed via loogle) but no SVD factorization and no Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse anywhere in Mathlib or Causalean (leansearch `Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of a matrix` returns only `Matrix.inv` for square nonsingular matrices). The Gram-matrix route is the standard equivalent construction and needs only `Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvectorUnitary` / `eigenvalues`, which Mathlib has. ROUND-4 CHANGE OF STATUS: this file is no longer definition-only. Because the former open question is now the delivered theorem thm:no-uniform-studentized-wald-adaptation, `phi_{r0}` acquires genuine PROOF obligations -- the note's localization step needs `phi_1` and `D phi_1` to be `C^1` with bounded derivative in a neighbourhood of the explicit rank-one `H_{x,0} = ((1/4,1/4),(1/4,1/4))`, whose Gram eigenvalues are `1/4` and `0` and hence strictly separated. At the 2x2 size actually used by the theorem the two roots of the characteristic polynomial have a closed form whose discriminant is bounded away from zero on that neighbourhood, so the smoothness is elementary Mathlib analysis (`Polynomial` roots / `Real.sqrt` differentiability away from 0) rather than a general analytic-perturbation theory; the general-`m` statement is not needed and is not planned. Still build-inline, still `defer_tier: false`: finite-dimensional, self-contained, no missing upstream theory. Effort rises from medium to large.

decisions.decision: The sampling worlds see the SCM only through EXPLICIT `Measure` conversions of its normalized finite laws, built at the head of `Helpers/Sampling.lean` from the F1-D1 normalization fields: `noncomputable def observedPMF (Mdl) : PMF (E x W x X x Y) := PMF.ofFintype (fun o => ENNReal.ofReal (observedLaw Mdl o.1 o.2.1 o.2.2.1 o.2.2.2)) h`, where `h` is discharged from `observedLaw_nonneg` and `observedLaw_sum`; `noncomputable def observedMeasure (Mdl) : Measure (E x W x X x Y) := (observedPMF Mdl).toMeasure`, a probability measure by `PMF.toMeasure.isProbabilityMeasure`; and identically `targetProxyPMF` / `targetProxyMeasure (Mdl) : Measure W` from `targetProxyVector`. Three bridge lemmas tie the samples back to the SCM's own moments: `observedMeasure_apply_singleton` and `targetProxyMeasure_apply_singleton` (from `PMF.toMeasure_apply_fintype` + `PMF.ofFintype_apply`), and the population-mean identity `integral_cellIndicator`, stating that the Bochner integral of the indicator of the cell `(e,w,x,y)` against `observedMeasure Mdl` equals `observedLaw Mdl e w x y` (with its `W`-side twin for `targetProxyVector`), proved by `PMF.integral_eq_sum` plus `Finset.sum_ite_eq`. The three empirical moments are then the finite `Fin ns` / `Fin nt` averages of exactly those indicators (ROUND-8, F1-D20: this single finite form replaces the round-6 dual presentation; `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample.sampleMean` survives only inside the proof of the helper `pi_hoeffding_cell`), so `hat H_x`, `hat z_{x,y}`, `hat b` are the empirical means of statistics whose population means ARE `H_x(w,e)`, `z_{x,y}(e)`, `b_w`. The five index types carry `[MeasurableSpace .] [MeasurableSingletonClass .]` instance binders in the sampling and triangular-array files only (satisfied by the discrete sigma-algebra on a `Fintype`); the pure-algebra files (FiniteSCM, Fibers, Basic, Perturbation, Witness, TruncatedSVD) import no measure theory. Finally `observedMeasure_congr : observedLaw M = observedLaw M' -> observedMeasure M = observedMeasure M'` (and its target twin) transports the conversion across `compatibleFiber` membership, so all models in one fiber sample from literally the same measure.
decisions.why: `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample Omega X mu P` takes the population law as `P : Measure X` (Stat/Sample.lean:44-50) and `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.hoeffding_abs_ge` centers the sample mean at the integral of the statistic against that same `P` (Stat/Concentration/TailBounds/Hoeffding.lean:167-171). Without an explicit conversion, S1's `observedLaw` and `targetProxyVector` are raw real arrays while the i.i.d. samples of S2/S3 hang off an unrelated measure: the empirical moments would concentrate around a population mean with no formal link to `H_x`, `z_{x,y}` or `b`, and thm:finite-sample-projection-coverage would prove coverage of a quantity unrelated to the SCM's causal query. `integral_cellIndicator` is the keystone that makes the centering constant of `hoeffding_abs_ge` equal the SCM moment; it is elementary and build-inline. `PMF.ofFintype`, `PMF.ofFintype_apply`, `PMF.toMeasure`, `PMF.toMeasure.isProbabilityMeasure`, `PMF.toMeasure_apply_fintype` and `PMF.integral_eq_sum` were all confirmed present (loogle `PMF.ofFintype`; leansearch `integral with respect to the measure of a PMF on a fintype equals a finite sum`).

decisions.decision: Every object whose meaning depends on inverting the normal CDF binds the error level in the core-declared domain as `alpha : Set.Ioo (0:Real) 1` (a subtype binder, coerced where a bare real is needed), never as a raw `alpha : Real`. env.world: A finite latent-shift structural causal model. The state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) are finite, with \(\mathcal E,\mathcal X\) nonempty, \(2\le r=\lvert\mathcal U\rvert\), \(m=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert\ge r\) and \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\ge2\). A model \(\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q)\) consists of a strictly positive environment law \(\pi\in\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal E)\), a strictly positive column-stochastic latent channel \(S\in\mathbb R^{r\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\) with \(S_{ue}=P(U=u\mid E=e)\), a strictly positive column-stochastic proxy channel \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) with \(M_{wu}=P(W=w\mid U=u)\), a strictly positive treatment kernel \(a_x(u)=P(X=x\mid U=u)\), a strictly positive outcome kernel \(f_{x,y}(u,w)=P(Y=y\mid U=u,W=w,X=x)\), and a strictly positive target latent mixture \(q\in\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal U)\); it induces the source full-data law \(P_{\mathcal M}\) on \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) and the target law \(Q_{\mathcal M}\) on \(\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\), Markov relative to \(\mathcal G\). env.world: The strongly identified regular submodel and its Wald benchmark, together with the ambient set geometry on \([0,1]\). For a rank index \(1\le r_0\le\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\) and constants \(c,\eta>0\), a generic moment matrix \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\) and outcome-moment vector \(z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\) determine the ordered singular-value functional \(\sigma_{r_0}\), with the convention \(\sigma_{\bar q+1}=0\) for \(\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\); a selector-based at-most-\(r_0\) Gram-spectral truncation \(H_{r_0}=P^{\star}_{r_0}(H)H\), where \(P^{\star}_{r_0}(H)\) projects onto the span of the first \(r_0\) vectors of one fixed, possibly noncomputable orthonormal eigenbasis of \(HH^{\top}\) ordered by nonincreasing eigenvalue, with one fixed choice inside every tied eigenspace; and the rank-\(r_0\) Wald functional \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b\), which is therefore single valued everywhere and, on the strict-cutoff-gap region \(\sigma_{r_0}(H)>\sigma_{r_0+1}(H)\), independent of the within-tie choice. Under independent source and target multinomial sampling with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\), \(\phi_{r_0}\) has population delta-method variance \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\), defined on that gap region only. The fixed strongly identified submodel \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}\subseteq\mathfrak M_{+}\) collects the models with \(\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0\), \(\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c\), \(b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x)\), all source and target cells at least \(\eta\), and \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta\); every such model lies in the gap region, since \(\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0\) forces \(\sigma_{r_0+1}(H_x)=0<c\le\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\).
